description: Stoa's content-addressed block store (CIDv1 SHA-256 DAG-CBOR) is the natural backend for JMAP FileNode (draft-ietf-jmap-filenode). FileNode is a named reference to a blob with metadata (MIME type, size, parent directory, permissions) — a thin indexing layer on top of what stoa already has. The hard part (content-addressed blob storage, upload/download, CID-based references) is done. Need: FileNode data type, FileNode/get, /set, /changes, /query, /queryChanges methods, directory hierarchy, and the urn:ietf:params:jmap:filenode capability. Stoa's existing jmap-cid capability (urn:stoa:jmap:cid) already exposes CIDs to clients, which complements FileNode's sha256 field from draft-atwood-jmap-cid-00.
title: Implement JMAP FileNode on top of CID block store
